# Queue-lane history for the drain.pg2 type and its drain-pg2 role, 2026-10-13 14:50Z .. 23:00Z: the account usage limit
# declined every drain-pg2 dispatch from 20:54:26Z to 21:59:59Z (pg2-9nfla). Replayed by queue_stalled_test.go and
# queue_slow_growth_test.go. Same record kinds as drain_pg2_2026-10-12.txt (E, X, D, S), plus B and R.
#
# REAL RECORDING, no synthesis. B, E, X and D are read from the pg-router durable queue log
# (~/.local/state/pg-router/queue.jsonl: enqueue, evict and accept records, and the archive records a compaction folds a
# departed event into); R is read from the daemon log (~/.local/state/pg-router/launchd-stderr.log, whose clock is local
# time, UTC-4 that day). Only timestamps are kept (UTC, to the second): event ids, bead ids and payloads are dropped.
#
# Record kinds, one per line (B and S first, then E, X and D in time order, then every R):
#   B <t> <n>      the lane held n events at <t>, the start of the recording. They are not arrivals: pg_router_enqueued_total
#                  was born at the 14:52:09Z apply, so no E record precedes <t>.
#   E <t>          an event was admitted (an arrival, as the new counter counts it). During the storm each decline retires a
#                  born-expired drain event and the source re-emits it on its next tick: the re-emission is an E again.
#   X <t>          an event left the queue (archive evictedAt or evict record): depth falls by one.
#   D <start> <t>  one ACCEPTED dispatch: the offer went in flight at <start> and settled at <t>, which is when
#                  pg_router_throughput_total advanced. The D records start 6 hours before <B>, so a 6 hour completions
#                  window is complete from the first evaluation (only the archived events of the queue log survive, which
#                  can omit an older dispatch).
#   R <t>          one DECLINED offer: the daemon logged `dispatch declined: ... role=drain-pg2` at <t> (the second the line
#                  carries). An offer is in flight from the moment it is made until it settles, and a decline is decided
#                  inside the offer (the handler's admission gate), so the role counts as in flight for a couple of seconds
#                  around <t> without anything being accepted. The offer is not accepted: no D record, no throughput.
#                  A replay models the span as [t-2s, t+1s) (queue_stalled_test.go, declineBefore and declineAfter).
#   S <from> <to>  the host was asleep: no router activity and no Prometheus scrape in [from, to) (gaps of 10 minutes or
#                  more in the router event log, ~/.local/state/pg-router/events.jsonl; the dark wakes inside them are not
#                  modelled).
#
# Facts a replay can be checked against (all read from the same records):
#   * 20:53:50Z is the last accept before the storm and 22:02:39Z the first after it; the dispatch that ended there went in
#     flight at 22:00:10Z, 11 seconds after the last decline (21:59:59Z), so nothing was processed for 66 minutes and the
#     lane held 19 to 24 events throughout. The dispatch in flight at 22:29:40Z (settled 23:17:41Z) has no D record: D
#     records are the dispatches that settled by 23:00Z, so a replay of the stalled rule stops at 22:29:00Z.
#   * 22 arrivals and 4 recorded accepts from 14:52Z to 20:52Z (depth 19 -> 35); from 20:54Z the storm adds one arrival
#     per decline.
#   * the Prometheus samples of pg_router_listener_in_flight{role="drain-pg2"} that read 1 inside the storm (the scrapes
#     are on :14 and :44 of every minute) were 21:15:44Z, 21:16:14Z, 21:21:14Z, 21:29:14Z and 21:33:44Z. Each has an R
#     record 0, 1 or 2 seconds after it, and the offsets of the model above reproduce all five.
